title: Scaling and Population Loss in Mexican Urban Centres
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75780-5

We analysed urban growth dynamics in 69 Mexican metropolitan areas from 1990 to 2020 using radial scaling analysis. In 30 years, the urban population shifted outwards, with all central zones losing 2.5 million people, absorbed by the peripheries.

title: Anchoring mechanism-inspired discovery of a bacterial P450 gene conferring resistance to auxin herbicides
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75811-1

The rapid evolution of herbicide-resistant weeds necessitates new resistance traits to sustain control efficacy. Here the authors discover and engineer a bacterial P450 peroxygenase that degrades auxin herbicides, and create a transgenic rice resistant to a commercialized auxin herbicide.

title: Substituent-rebound skeletal editing for precise boron-to-carbon single-atom swapping
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75992-9

Developing methods that enable single-atom exchange within an aromatic scaffold, while preserving its peripheral substitution, represents an important but highly ambitious goal in synthesis. Here the authors present a boron-to-carbon swapping reaction via a substituent-rebound process, converting 1,2-benzazaborines into the corresponding quinolines.

title: Semiconductor room-temperature maser
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75446-2

The first semiconductor maser in silicon carbide is demonstrated, achieving continuous-wave operation above room temperature with high gain, microwave mode cooling, and ultrasensitive magnetometry, enabling compact, scalable maser technologies.

title: Navigating optimal solar-wind trade-offs under climate change
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75879-9

This study finds that climate change modestly alters optimal solar-wind ratios, whereas deployment pathways that diverge from climate-consistent optimal ratios can substantially increase electricity supply costs and capacity needs across regions.

title: Counteranion-mediated dynamic kinetic asymmetric fluorination to access sulfur-stereogenic center
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76036-y

The authors present a highly efficient strategy to synthesize sulfonimidoyl fluorides through dynamic kinetic asymmetric fluorination at mild reaction conditions. This one-pot process, involving sequential direct fluorination, hydrolysis, and asymmetric fluorination, delivers a wide range of enantioenriched S(VI) compounds with high enantioselectivities.

title: Hydroxyl‑Mediated SO<sub>2</sub> Promotion Enables Efficient NO<sub>x</sub> Reduction by CO over IrIn/Beta under Oxygen‑Rich Conditions
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76010-8

Removing NOx from oxygen-rich industrial flue gas is difficult, especially with SO2 present. An IrIn/Beta catalyst turns SO2 into ammonium sulfate intermediates, promoting NOx high removal under harsh simulated industrial conditions.

title: Serpentine’s wet breakdown path and enhanced water flux in cold subduction zones
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75935-4

Extra water in cold tectonic plates causes sinking rocks (serpentinites) to transform and absorb more water. This boosts deep water transport by cold slabs, creating lateral contrasts in hydration, density, and seismic velocity.
